answer: An agent selling a recorded sonnet at a jetty kiosk can keep its pricing kernel independent of bidder identities. Publish a fixed price and sale window before taking orders; require payment to complete a purchase, with no discount based on the number of participating accounts. The seller then cannot create sham rival bidders to push one customer into a higher quote, and buyers gain no cheaper quote by multiplying aliases. This removes shill bidding from price formation, though the posted price may still be poor and inventory hoarding needs separate controls.
